boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort McAllister I record (March 3, 1863) in Naval Attacks on Fort McAllister [March 1863]. The January 27, February 1 and February 28 attacks on the fort, and the mortar fire of the night of March 3-4, are context. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text names the Union navy flotilla and the fort garrison; the live field reads zero. Drayton says his vessel lay under fire with Ammen and Downes in support, three mortar schooners firing from about 4,000 yards and three gunboats anchored near them; he judged the fort to contain seven guns and a mortar. McCrady describes three monitors in action, a fourth that took no part, one river and one ocean steamer and three mortar vessels, and names the fort's VIII-inch, X-inch and 42-pounder guns, a rifled 32-pounder, 32-pounders and a X-inch mortar; neither gives a garrison or crew strength.
claims.rationale: Vessel and gun counts only; no personnel figure. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Drayton says the fort stood at least 20 feet above the river with high traverses between the guns, that shallow water, a narrow channel and piles kept him about 1,200 yards off (the pilot called it a thousand), and that the natural obstacles made another attack as unlikely to succeed. McCrady puts the three ironclads at 1,400 to 1,900 yards, in the channel about 200 yards from the marsh opposite.
claims.rationale: Distances are the two sides' estimates and differ; no map verification. The earthwork predates the attack.

claims.value: Drayton learned the fort's earlier armament from a pilot who had deserted from it two months before. McCrady's report rests on McAlpin's notes and the officers' statements, and identifies the vessel under fire as the Montauk; a compiler's footnote in the printed report says the Montauk was not in action.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge on both sides; the misidentification is preserved as printed. No original reconnaissance, order or message chain was inspected to establish contemporary knowledge. Surprise in a summary does not independently establish what each commander knew.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Drayton says the attack was unsuccessful and that no injury was done that a good night's work would not repair; McCrady reports no material damage to the earthwork and the garrison as ready to fight again the next morning. McCrady's report dates the attack 'Tuesday, March 8' in OCR; the frozen date is March 3.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 1 total (US 0; CS 1). McCrady reports two men slightly wounded, one by a shell fragment and one by a sod peg, and one gun carriage destroyed. Drayton's reports list damage to the Passaic but no casualties.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Frozen 'Unknown', the live CS 1 and McCrady's two slightly wounded are preserved.

open_questions: Du Pont's March 6 transmittal, Miller's report of the Passaic's injuries, Ammen's and Downes's reports, the abstract logs, Harris's covering letter, Beauregard's March 3-4 dispatches (Official Records I, XIV) and Samuel Jones's chapter IX remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Percival Drayton's detailed report and his March 8, 1863 report to the Bureau of Ordnance (Official Records of the Navies I, 13) are interested Union accounts. John McCrady's report (printed in the same volume) is a Confederate engineer's compilation from McAlpin's notes and the garrison officers' statements. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
